title: The New Forever War
gist: Ali Vaez argues the American-Iranian war has become a 'new forever war' in which both sides fight on without victory: Trump predicts it will end right after the November election and IRGC chief Ahmad Vahidi claims Iran has brought the U.S. military to its knees, but many analysts expect a longer conflict. Only the opening is available (teaser).

insights.claim: President Trump said in September that the war with Iran will end immediately after the November election because Iran 'can't hold out any longer.'
insights.speaker: Ali Vaez
insights.so_what: Markets may be pricing a post-election de-escalation that the author doubts; downside risk to that assumption for oil and regional assets.
insights.quote: I think the war is going to end immediately after the [November] election
insights.locator: When will the war in Iran end?

insights.claim: IRGC commander in chief Ahmad Vahidi proclaimed in August that Tehran has brought the most heavily armed army in history to its knees, signalling Iranian leaders also see the war's end as near on their terms.
insights.speaker: Ali Vaez
insights.so_what: Both sides claiming victory reduces incentives for compromise.
insights.quote: brought the most heavily armed army in the history of the world to its knees
insights.locator: Iranian leaders agree that the war’s conclusion

insights.claim: Contrary to official claims, many outside analysts expect the American-Iranian conflict to drag on longer.
insights.speaker: Ali Vaez
insights.so_what: A protracted conflict implies sustained Gulf energy and shipping risk premia.
insights.quote: Many outside analysts think that the conflict will drag on for longer

insights.claim: Vaez frames the conflict as a 'new forever war' in which America and Iran fight on without either achieving victory.
insights.speaker: Ali Vaez
insights.so_what: Investors should treat Middle East conflict risk as structural rather than a near-term event to fade.
insights.quote: Why America and Iran Fight On Without Victory
